description:
Serbia’s student-led movement has dealt a major blow to President Aleksandar Vucic’s political dominance, winning a parliamentary election after nearly two years of protests demanding accountability and an end to corruption.

The movement gained momentum after a railway station roof collapsed in Novi Sad in November 2024, killing 16 people. Its campaign called for greater accountability and an end to political control of the public broadcaster.

As supporters celebrate in Belgrade, the movement faces the challenge of turning its election victory into lasting political change.

More than 2,000 Palestinians have been forcibly displaced during Israel’s assault on Hebron in the occupied West Bank, with almost half of them children.

Families describe fleeing their homes as Israeli forces carry out demolitions and impose movement restrictions. The report also documents an elderly Palestinian man being kicked by an Israeli soldier and shows residents helping business owners salvage what they can before demolitions.

Displacement is also affecting Palestinian communities near Jenin, where residents say they have been ordered to leave their village.

Al Jazeera Nour Odeh reports from the occupied West Bank.
title: Palestinians forced from homes as Israeli assault hits Hebron

description:
Marine Le Pen has launched her fourth bid for the French presidency in Orléans, presenting an optimistic vision for France despite controversy surrounding her policies and a recent conviction for embezzling public funds.

Her supporters say the National Rally leader offers solutions to immigration, the rising cost of living and insecurity. But her positions on cutting aid to Ukraine and banning headscarves have drawn opposition, with protests in Orléans and Paris highlighting the divisions surrounding her campaign.

Can Le Pen turn her support into a path to the presidency?

Al Jazeera's Rosie Birchard reports.
title: Marine Le Pen launches fourth bid for French presidency

description:
Vote counting is underway in Brazil’s closely contested presidential runoff, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leading right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro as more ballots are counted.

With 87% of the votes counted, Lula is nearly three percentage points ahead, according to Al Jazeera’s live report from Brasília. The result has surprised observers after Bolsonaro finished ahead in the first round earlier this month.

Journalists are waiting for Flávio Bolsonaro to address the results as counting continues. Questions remain over whether he will accept the outcome if Lula’s lead holds.

title: Brazil election: Lula takes lead as vote counting continues
